# What the data-dict export loses: Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), student questionnaire

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2012` | `2015` | `2018` | `2022` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 23 | 24 | 24 | 24 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 12 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 58 | 71 | 62 | 62 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| quantities exported with open range bounds (no valid range recorded) | 8 | 13 | 13 | 13 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 32 | 24 | 24 | 24 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 122 | 126 | 126 | 128 |
| groups (batteries, subjects, sections), not exported | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| links between releases, not exported | 46 | 46 | 46 | 46 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
